tagline.text: A protected reef off Mactan on the Olango Reef, an easy half-day snorkeling island trip

location.label: Location
location.text: Waters west of Gilutongan (Hilutungan) Island, Cordova, Cebu, on the Olango Reef east of Mactan Island

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~4,500 (per person, island tour basis; varies with group size)

children.text: Hilutungan Marine Sanctuary is a protected coral area west of Gilutongan Island, about 30 minutes by boat from Mactan Island, and a signature snorkeling stop on Cebu island-hopping tours. Its shallow, clear water makes it easy to see coral and tropical fish, which suits beginners and families.

Hilutungan Marine Sanctuary is a marine protected area within the Olango Reef, east of Mactan Island in Cebu and southwest of Olango Island. Administratively, it covers the waters west of Gilutongan Island (also spelled Hilutangan or Hilutungan), which belongs to the municipality of Cordova. The Olango group has six small satellite islets, and Gilutongan is known to be one of them, forming a single barangay together with neighboring Nalusuan Island. The sanctuary protects the coral beds off the island's west coast, so think of it as a place to look into the water rather than an island to lounge on a beach.

For travelers, it has become a standard stop on Cebu island-hopping tours. An outrigger boat from a Mactan resort or pier takes about 30 minutes, and the usual plan is to float over the shallow coral in a life vest. The water is shallow and calm on many days, so even non-swimmers often join in wearing a life vest, and family trips with children are common. Conditions do depend on the weather, so check first on the day whether boats are running.

It helps to set your expectations. Lonely Planet describes the snorkeling as not especially outstanding because of past reef damage, while several travel sites instead praise the clear water and variety of tropical fish. In short, this is not a place to compare with the Philippines' top dive sites; its main appeal is a protected reef that is easy to reach and can be visited in half a day from Mactan. Touching or stepping on coral is prohibited inside the sanctuary, and if you follow that rule, anyone can enjoy it comfortably.

You can reportedly see butterflyfish, clownfish, angelfish and parrotfish, along with sea anemones, soft corals and starfish. Some sources mention occasional sea turtles, but meeting one is a matter of luck, so it is best not to count on it.

blocks.title: Island tours linked to the Olango Reef

children.text: Hilutungan is often combined with nearby Nalusuan Island and Pandanon Island on a one-day route. Which islands are included differs by tour package, so be sure to check the stops before booking.

Some articles describe it as one of the oldest protected marine areas in Cebu, and a research source says Cordova adopted a protection ordinance in 1999. Remembering that this sea survives thanks to protection makes the trip more meaningful.

Snorkeling is the main activity, but scuba diving is also said to be possible. One travel article listed a snorkeling fee and a diving fee separately. Diving is mainly for experienced divers, and schedules and equipment need to be arranged separately with an operator.
It takes about
25–30 minutes

by boat from the Mactan resort area, so it works well as a morning outing with the afternoon free to rest at your hotel. If you are coming from Cebu City, just add the transfer time to Mactan and it is still a half-day trip.
Older travel accounts mention throwing bread to attract fish, but feeding, fishing and touching coral are generally prohibited in sanctuaries. Follow your guide's instructions and check local rules.

blocks.title: Combine with the Olango Wildlife Sanctuary

children.text: The Olango Island Wildlife Sanctuary is an area of tidal flats of about
1,020 hectares

designated by Proclamation No. 903 in May 1992 and registered as a Ramsar wetland in July 1994. July–November is said to be the best time to see migratory birds. A day linking the marine sanctuary and the bird wetland is possible, but transport and timing must be confirmed separately with an operator.

items.title: Half-day course from Mactan
items.subtitle: Morning snorkeling, then back to the hotel

children.text: Head to the outrigger boat boarding point near your Mactan resort or pier. Many sources say the morning sea is relatively calm and has fewer boats, so a morning departure is recommended.
The boat sets off toward Hilutungan. The trip is described as about
25–30 minutes
and varies with waves and wind.
The boat anchors at the sanctuary. Put on your life vest and snorkel gear, listen to the guide's briefing, and get in the water.
Snorkel slowly over the coral beds. In the water, adjust your swimming direction so you do not step on or touch the coral.
Get out of the water, rest on the boat and have a snack. There are reportedly no restrooms or shops on the island, so take care of that before departure.
If included in the tour, move on to a neighboring island (Nalusuan, Pandanon, etc.) or return to Mactan.
The schedule differs by operator. Check whether lunch is included and which islands are visited before booking.
Leave your Cebu City hotel for Mactan. Allow extra time because traffic is heavy at this hour.
Take the boat from the Mactan departure point to Hilutungan.
Snorkel at the sanctuary.
Move to another island (such as Nalusuan) for lunch and a rest.
Return to Mactan, then head back to the city.
If sea conditions worsen, the afternoon program may be shortened or canceled.
Several direct flights a day run from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB). The flight takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
The airport is on Mactan Island, close to the boat departure points for Hilutungan.
Flight schedules vary by season, so check the latest timetable.

items.title: From the airport or Cebu City to the Mactan pier

children.text: From Cebu City to the Mactan port, a taxi or Grab is reported to take about
45–60 minutes
. It varies greatly with traffic.
Hilton Port, Maribago and the Cordova area are mentioned as departure points. Confirm the place your booked operator designates.
From the Mactan resort area, an outrigger boat is said to take about
25–30 minutes
Both group island-hopping tours and private boat charters are available; a private charter gives you a flexible schedule but costs more.
Many sources say December–May, the dry season with calm seas and good visibility, is best for snorkeling. However, boats and crowds increase in peak periods such as December, April and Holy Week.

Within the day, 8 AM–11 AM is described as having calmer seas, fewer boats and better light. Afternoons can be windy or crowded. Tours may be canceled when a typhoon or low-pressure area approaches, so check the forecast.

There reportedly are no restrooms or restaurants at the Hilutungan sanctuary, so check whether lunch and water are included in the tour and bring your own snacks and water to be safe. Lunch is usually eaten on a neighboring island or after returning to Mactan.

The Mactan resort area is close to the boat departure points and convenient. You can also make the trip from a Cebu City hotel, but allow for the transfer time. There is information that a resort exists on Gilutongan Island, but rates and operating status need to be confirmed locally.

Fishing and boat operations are described as a main source of income for residents around Olango and Gilutongan. Since tour fees support local residents and sanctuary management, it is better for everyone to agree on a reasonable price rather than haggle excessively. Lunch is commonly seafood such as grilled fish, shrimp, squid and shellfish, but it differs by operator, so tell them in advance if you have allergies.
Before booking a tour, check whether the sanctuary fee is included and what is arranged for gear and lunch.
It is safer to wear a life vest even if you are a strong swimmer.
To protect the coral, we recommend reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard.
A waterproof pouch or action camera makes it easier to take photos.
If you get seasick, take motion-sickness medicine before boarding.
Morning trips tend to have calmer seas and fewer people.
Take your trash back with you and cut down on plastic bags.
Carry small peso bills for fees and tips.
Combining Hilutungan and Olango Island on the same day lengthens travel and makes the schedule tight, so focusing on one is more relaxed.
This is a local fishing community, so ask residents for permission before taking their photos.
Touching or stepping on coral, feeding fish and fishing are generally prohibited in the sanctuary, and violations may carry fines.
Boats may be canceled on rough-sea days or when a typhoon approaches, so check on the morning of your trip whether tours are running.
